title: Follow the Activity Before the Molecule

scenes.tts: You cannot purify what you cannot detect. A tumor in an embryo is a slow, messy detector. So Levi Montalcini moved the test into a dish. She set a chick ganglion in a clot of blood plasma. Then she placed a fragment of tumor near it, not touching.
scenes.caption: You cannot purify what you cannot detect. A tumor in an embryo is a slow, messy detector. So Levi-Montalcini moved the test into a dish. She set a chick ganglion in a clot of blood plasma. Then she placed a fragment of tumor near it, not touching.
scenes.visual: A tumor-in-an-embryo box labelled slow, messy detector turns into a dish. A ganglion in a plasma clot appears, then a tumor fragment with a gap beside the clot.
scenes.narration: You cannot purify what you cannot detect. A tumor in an embryo is a slow, messy detector. So Levi-Montalcini moved the test into a dish. She set a chick ganglion in a clot of blood plasma. Then she placed a fragment of tumor near it, not touching.

scenes.tts: Within 24 hours, the ganglion put out a dense halo of fibers. The halo was thickest toward the tumor. The whole experiment now fit in a dish. That halo is a bioassay. It uses a living response as the measuring device, so it works before you know what the molecule is.
scenes.visual: Fibers grow from the ganglion, longer and denser on the tumor side. The halo is named a bioassay. A question mark appears on the tumor fragment: the molecule is unknown.
scenes.narration: Within 24 hours, the ganglion put out a dense halo of fibers. The halo was thickest toward the tumor. The whole experiment now fit in a dish. That halo is a bioassay. It uses a living response as the measuring device, so it works before you know what the molecule is.

scenes.tts: A bioassay can also be quantitative. Dilute a sample step by step. The highest dilution that still gives a halo tells you how much factor the sample holds. Divide by the milligrams of protein in the sample. That gives the specific activity: the activity per milligram of protein.
scenes.visual: A row of tubes, each paler than the last. Each is tested on a ganglion: halos on the first three, none on the last two. The last halo is boxed. Then activity divided by milligrams of protein gives specific activity.
scenes.narration: A bioassay can also be quantitative. Dilute a sample step by step. The highest dilution that still gives a halo tells you how much factor the sample holds. Divide by the milligrams of protein in the sample. That gives the specific activity: the activity per milligram of protein.

scenes.tts: Now test a sample from each purification step with the same assay. Every step is judged by one question. Did the activity per milligram go up? The assay lets you follow the factor before you know what it is. So keep this rule: you cannot purify what you cannot detect.
scenes.visual: Three tubes joined by purification-step arrows, each tested on a ganglion with a halo. The question appears: did the activity per milligram go up? The assay row glows as the factor is followed.
